chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So if you fear, [then pray] on foot or riding' — how should we pray? And what should one say if he fears from a beast of prey or a thief? How should he pray? He said: 'He should say Takbir and gesture with his head.'
ai.seo_question: How does one perform prayer when fearing an enemy or danger according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanics of Salat al-Khawf, establishing that when fear prevents physical bowing (ruku) and prostration (sujood), the believer may substitute them with head gestures (iima') while maintaining the Takbir. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'ease in difficulty' (taysir), ensuring the prayer remains valid even in extreme combat or danger scenarios, as referenced in the broader context of Surah al-Nisa. The emphasis on head gestures rather than full bodily prostration underscores the flexibility of ritual acts when physical capability is compromised by external threats.
